INCAPACITATED path requires RAM approvals AND min(ceil(0.7g),5) guardian approvals on ONE access request (p.225782 step 7; Alg.3 p.225786); EMERGENCY path requires RAM approvals AND hospital admission confirmation. No single party can authorize; guardians capped at 5 (Alg.2). This is N-of-M over independent parties, not delegation/substitution, and not blockchain consensus (S27-3/4 not triggered). T5=YES: expiry is ENFORCED inside the decision predicate — isClaimVerified counts a verification only "if now - claim.dates_i <= claim.oldestDate" (Alg.1 p.225785); stale attestations silently stop counting. T6=YES: explicit revokeClaim by a prior verifier + removeGuardian retracting guardianship (Alg.1/Alg.2 p.225785) + timed auto-invalidation + renewal — four transitions with decision effect. LIMIT: no named state machine; post-delivery revocation impossible (PRE + off-chain hand-off). T4=PARTIAL: request-type branching + role gating + per-document (IPFS hash) scope do affect the decision, but this is hardcoded control flow, not a policy model. ABSENCE TEST on full text: "purpose"=0, "policy"=0 (in body), "FHIR"=0, "HL7"=0, "Synthea"=0, "dataset"=0 hits. ABAC appears only as related-work critique (pp.225778-779). Req6=NO by absence test: "formal"=0, "adversary"=0, "theorem"=0, "model checking"=0 occurrences. SIV-C (p.225788) is qualitative prose (authenticity/confidentiality/integrity/availability/non-repudiation) with no adversary model, no property statement, no proof. Req7=PARTIAL: real executed artefact (Solidity 0.6.12, JS-EVM testnet, 13 accounts Table 1 p.225786; gas+USD Table 2 p.225788; one negative-path tx Fig.4) BUT no dataset, no attack tests, no ALLOW/DENY correctness matrix, no latency/throughput, no interoperability, no usability; GitHub link anonymised (anon092020/PHR-MPA). === CHAIR ADVERSARIAL FINDING (A3+A5, key-custody asymmetry) === Guardians hold NO key shares. The IPFS private key is split 3 (agency) + 3 (patient) (p.225781), and p.225782 step 10 states the regulatory agency nodes "independently use their 3 shares and decrypt the medical document private key". Therefore the threshold cryptography is patient/agency key escrow in which ONE institution holds a sufficient share set; the genuine MPA is the ON-CHAIN claim-verification gate, not the cryptographic gate. SIV-C p.225788 asserts that sharing without patient consent requires the MPA parties "to collaborate maliciously" — that guarantee holds at the smart-contract layer only. The paper title claim "Fully Decentralized" is ASSERTED, not demonstrated: the regulatory agency is sole identity verifier, mandatory MPA participant on both non-patient paths, and sole holder of a decrypt-capable share set. This is precisely the class of defect an unverified conjunctive predicate conceals — it strengthens deficit 2 on evidence, not by rhetoric.

T3 was No 8/8; now Yes 1/9 — the "multi-party joint authorization does not exist" line is FALSIFIED and must be retracted from CA2. WHAT SURVIVES: (i) MPA here is a CONTINGENCY path conditioned on principal absence (INCAPACITATED/EMERGENCY); on the normal path (t=PATIENT) a single patient key authorizes (Alg.3 p.225786) — so multi-party approval is an availability fallback, not a constitutive predicate on every consent decision. (ii) The strongest T3 system in the corpus has ZERO formal assurance (Req6=No by absence test) — deficit 2 becomes the primary defensible novelty locus. (iii) purpose/data-category policy remains absent (0/9) — deficit 4 hardens. (iv) The key-custody asymmetry shows the joint guarantee is contract-enforced, not cryptographically enforced, and is nowhere verified.

note: PRE-REGISTERED TEST 1 (ATS scope) — RESULT: SPLIT, hence T3=PARTIAL not Yes. The (t,n) ATS genuinely runs over independent named human roles and is NOT Fabric consensus, so S27-3/4 does NOT apply: investigators hold distinct yes/no key pairs, sign shares, and a combiner recovers fsig (pp.8-9). BUT what it gates is asymmetric: (a) TRIAL WRITE-ADMISSION — "the consensus node can determine if this message m (a patient trial) can be submitted to the Blockchain ledger or not" (p.9) and "a trial needs to be certified by a majority of the investigators" (p.6). That is ledger admission / data governance, not a patient data-access decision. (b) CONSENT REVOCATION — "Patient consent can be revoked by the admins or the patient, but it needs to be approved by half of the investigators" (p.8). This IS a multi-party gate on a consent LIFECYCLE TRANSITION. (c) CONSENT GRANT — unilateral: "Patients can submit their consents through user interfaces to grant the permit to experimenters or researchers" (p.10). No threshold. THEREFORE: multi-party gates revocation and record admission, NOT the grant. ADVERSARIAL FINDING (A3+A5): the threshold VOTE reduces to an INTEGRITY CHECK, not an authorization judgment — Step 3 p.8: investigators "check the content of the message m (e.g., recalculate hash code of m, h*(m)). If a member ci confirms that this message is valid (h(m)==h*(m))" then signs. A threshold of hash-verifiers is not a threshold of authorizers. Additional distinction from IEEE-1069: investigators are INSTITUTION-SIDE (footnote 1 p.5: "an individual who conducts a clinical investigation" — attending doctors, directors), not patient-side guardians. TEST 2 (S27-5): passed as applied — threshold is over message admission, which is why Req3 is Partial and not Yes. TEST 3 (S27-3/4): FPC/SGX enclave execution and Fabric BFT finality are infrastructure and are NOT counted; the ATS is a separate protocol layer. Clean. TEST 4 (Req6): FAILED — no theorem, no proof, no adversary model, no model checking, no security definition for ATS. S6.2 (p.13) is prose on SGX attack surface and TEE statelessness. Req6=No. T5=PARTIAL under S27-8: "All the consents have a start time and an end time for legal access" (p.8) is a stored attribute; no predicate, algorithm or test demonstrates time gating the decision. T6=YES: explicit enumerated states Approved/Pending/Completed/Revoked with investigator-verified transitions (p.8) and implemented endpoints Consent Grant / Consent Revoke / Consent Acknowledge (Table 1 p.12). T4=PARTIAL but notable: consent is bound to a STUDY NUMBER and validated at an endpoint ("Consent Validate StudyNumber", Table 1 p.12) — a real purpose-scope anchor in a deployed system; still no policy engine, no attributes, no data-category scope. TERMINOLOGY FINDING for SLR-RQ1: the title claims "Trust Computing" but the paper never defines a trust model; here "trust computing" denotes TRUSTED HARDWARE (SGX/TEE). Record as corpus terminology drift, not as a defence of our framing.

venue: Computer Standards & Interfaces, vol. 93, art. 103967 (2025); Beijing Jiaotong University
note: PRE-REGISTERED TEST 1 (what do the authorization proofs prove?) — PASSED, and strongly. AutProof is a NIZK PoK over the conjunction {Com_HID = sk*H + hid_o*G AND Token = hid_o*pk_c} (Alg.6, p.9). The second conjunct binds the authorization to a SPECIFIC EMR Queryer public key, so the proof establishes that this data subject deliberately authorised THIS requester — not merely that the subject exists. VerAut (Alg.7, p.10) checks that the owner being queried is the owner who authorised the queryer, WITHOUT learning the owner identity. This is genuine data-subject authorization, cleanly separated from authentication (which is the DID challenge-response, Appendix). Strongest Req2 in the corpus. PRE-REGISTERED TEST 2 (is "multi-party" authorizing parties?) — FAILED. T3 = No. §27-21 NEW WORD SENSE: here "multi-party" denotes MULTIPLE STAKEHOLDERS WHOSE COMPETING PRIVACY REQUIREMENTS ARE SIMULTANEOUSLY SATISFIED (RQ1 Queryer privacy, RQ2 Provider privacy, RQ3 Owner privacy, RQ4 Producer privacy — p.2), NOT multiple parties jointly authorising one decision. Authorization is issued by ONE EMR Owner alone with their own sk (Alg.6). No threshold, no N-of-M, no guardian, no co-consent anywhere in the construction. "Threshold" appears only in the related-work critique of Zhao et al. [24] and in cited preliminary [47] Stinson-Strobl, which is NOT used. PRE-REGISTERED TEST 3 (does the Formal signal correspond to real proofs?) — PASSED. Req6 = YES, THE FIRST IN THE CORPUS. Three game-based security definitions with PPT adversary and oracle access (S4.3, pp.7-8), three theorems with reduction proofs (S6, pp.11-12): Thm 6.1 anonymity <- Pedersen hiding; Thm 6.2 unforgeability of authorization proof <- ECDLP via Forking Lemma with explicit bound; Thm 6.3 search privacy <- ECDDH. Plus completeness/soundness/zero-knowledge of AutProof (Eqs.12-14) and a negligibility bound on the keyword-collision event (Eq.15). Standard assumptions formalised in S3.1 (Eqs.1-3). This is complete cryptographic formal assurance. PRE-REGISTERED TEST 4 (does DID establish authority or only identity?) — authority, via the Token binding above. §27-13 not triggered. === CHAIR: WHAT IS PROVEN vs WHAT IS NOT === The three theorems cover ANONYMITY, UNFORGEABILITY and SEARCH PRIVACY. There is NO theorem of the form "access is granted only if [conditions]". Unforgeability proves an adversary cannot FABRICATE a proof; it says nothing about the scope a valid proof confers. Crucially, the proofs CANNOT cover policy, temporal or lifecycle conjuncts BECAUSE HEALTHDID HAS NONE: T4 No (no purpose, no role, no data category; access is all-or-nothing per authorising owner; "scope" in S9.2 means the set of authorising owners, i.e. the identity dimension again). T5 No under §27-8 — the only time artefacts are TS used to build index_p = H2(TS, DID_p), a retrieval index for the Regulator, and IssuanceDate/ExpirationDate in the illustrative W3C DID document (Fig.A.9); no algorithm reads either. DID "regular update" is key rotation for unlinkability, not authorization expiry. T6 No — HealthDID has NO revocation, NO withdrawal, NO states, NO renewal. "Revocation" appears only in the related-work critique of Xu et al. [19]. The challenge-response value v (S6.1.2) gives per-query freshness against replay, which is anti-replay, not lifecycle state management. Req7 Partial: rigorous and reproducible PERFORMANCE evaluation (public repo, Curve25519, exact hardware and network conditions, parameter sweeps n1 2^4..2^12 and n2 2^10..2^20, four baselines) but NO ALLOW/DENY correctness suite, NO executed attack tests (S6.1 is analytical), NO dataset, no FHIR/HL7, no usability, LAN-only by the authors own statement. §27-19 flag: Tables 1 and 4 are self-scored feature matrices in which HealthDID scores a tick on every column; S8.1 "evaluation" is Table 4 alone.
gap: NARROWS (D2) — DEFICIT 2 BROKEN IN ITS ABSOLUTE FORM, RESTATED SHARPER. Req6 Yes is now 1/11 (was 0/10). CA2 may no longer say formal assurance is absent from this literature. WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS STRONGER THAN WHAT IT REPLACES: HealthDID proves anonymity, unforgeability and search privacy — properties of the IDENTITY/AUTHORITY FRAGMENT ONLY. It cannot prove policy, temporal or lifecycle properties because it implements none (T4/T5/T6 all No). OBSERVED INVERSE RELATION across 11 coded studies: formal assurance strength varies INVERSELY with predicate breadth. IEEE-1069 (T3 Yes, T5 Yes, T6 Yes) -> Req6 No. SCOPUS-1721 (T3 Partial, T6 Yes) -> Req6 No. SCOPUS-0570 (Req6 Yes, full game-based proofs) -> implements only VI AND VA. NO STUDY OCCUPIES THE UPPER-RIGHT QUADRANT: broad predicate AND formal assurance. That is a POSITIVE, evidence-grounded claim about the corpus and it replaces the old absence claim entirely. It is the strongest finding of the review so far and it is exactly the HALAH slot. DEFICIT 1 unaffected; T3 tally now Yes 1 / Partial 1 / No 9. INTELLIGENCE: HealthDID related work (p.2) describes Zhao et al. [24] = SCOPUS-1208 (Comput. Secur. 139:103686, 2024) as enabling "EMR owners to entrust multiple authorized EMR Queryers to complete authorization in a threshold-based manner" with responsibility threshold signatures, criticised for a centralized authorization center. Independent Q1 corroboration that SCOPUS-1208 is a genuine threshold-authorization scheme, not a word-sense artefact. It moves to rank 1 in the T3 batch.
